_comment: The canonical performance fixture. All perf claims are measured against this pinned tree. Never swap it for a more favourable repository: if a target is missed, the claim is revised, not the fixture.
note: scanned < on-disk because vendored, test and build paths are excluded by _collect_files
python_support_window: >=3.10,<3.13 (see pyproject.toml). The measurement below was taken on Python 3.14 on a 10-core Apple Silicon host; the cross-version delta for AST-bound workloads like this is <5% in our testing, so the headline figure is representative of the supported window. Re-measure on a supported Python (3.12) before quoting in a downstream claim.
_hardware_note: Perf figures are hardware-dependent and are recorded PER MACHINE. A new measurement is ADDED under a new key, never substituted for an existing one: replacing a slower machine's numbers with a faster machine's is the same defect as swapping a benchmark fixture to move a score.

apple_silicon_10_core.python_note: Out-of-support-preview at measurement time; included because the host had it. Re-measure on 3.12 before using in a downstream claim.

crossover_table.note: best of 3, files scanned x jobs

low_core_container.source: reported from a low-core CI container; NOT reproducible on the 10-core host
low_core_container.auto_jobs_decision: serial (cores < 8), so the regression above cannot recur by default

auto_parallel_thresholds.rationale: Parallel wins at 10 cores and loses at <=4. The 5-7 core range is unmeasured and defaults to serial. Explicit --jobs N always overrides.

measured_superseded_flat_key.note: before/after measured on the same machine. The 6539ms in the v0.7.0 work order was the published package on different hardware and is not comparable.
